subject: Compile-Time Arithmetic (Mode of arithmetic used and rules for intermediate data handling)
notes: Documented System.Decimal mode, COBOL-2023 only (kb/Work PB1592): 2/3*3=2, 100/7*7=100, 1/3*3=0, ties to even 2.5E-28->2, 7.5E-28->8, GR3 truncation; overflow COBOL1547/1619. Annex E.2 6) makes the mode implementor-defined only at 2023 and records that 'The previous COBOL Standard required the use of an arithmetic mode that is no longer supported' (cite.py --check E.2 -> OK §E.2 6)); the only mode 2023 removed is Standard Arithmetic (-> OK §E.2 21)), so at 2002/2014 the mode is PRESCRIBED, not this determination: CompileTimeArithmetic.For selects standard arithmetic (the SDIDI engine, 34 digits, NEAREST-AWAY-FROM-ZERO) below 2023 through DialectBehavior.CompileTimeArithmeticImplementorDefined (VCR row 12), witnessed by conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb1592_ct_arith_standard and the confirmed INV-3 variant arithmetic-intermediate-precision-2023. GnuCOBOL 3.2 survey (sources read, not copied): cobc folds literal-only binary operations with 64-bit integers and has no >>IF arithmetic evaluator - narrower than System.Decimal, so the 2023 choice stands.
